title: Pacoima on I-5: Exit 155, Ritchie Valens' Hometown
meta: Pacoima sits at exit 155 on I-5, hometown of Ritchie Valens, with listed gas, food and EV charging at nearby exits. A talking guide from I-5 Buddy.
intro: Pacoima is at exit 155 on I-5, in the north San Fernando Valley with Mission Hills and Sylmar. Its name comes from Pakoinga, a Native village name meaning entrance, and it is the hometown of Ritchie Valens, born Richard Valenzuela here in 1941. I-5 Buddy's talking guide covers the exits and stops around town, as mapped in OpenStreetMap data and not live.

faq.q: What exit is Pacoima on I-5?
faq.a: The Pacoima landmark is at exit 155, with exit 155A at Terra Bella Street and exit 155B at Van Nuys Boulevard.
The name comes from Pakoinga, a Native village here whose name means entrance. Spanish ears heard its ng sound as an m.
Ritchie Valens, born Richard Valenzuela in Pacoima in 1941. In 1958 he turned the Mexican folk song La Bamba into a rock and roll hit.

faq.q: Where can I get gas and food near Pacoima on I-5?
faq.a: Gas and food are listed at several nearby exits, including 154 (Osborne Street), 155A (Terra Bella Street) and 155B (Van Nuys Boulevard), where 7 food places are mapped. Exit 157 in San Fernando lists the most gas stations, 8, as mapped and not live.

faq.q: Is there an EV charger near Pacoima on I-5?
faq.a: EVgo is listed at exit 154 (Osborne Street). A Tesla Supercharger is listed at exit 157, and exit 157B lists Tesla and other EV chargers, as mapped and not live.
